limitations: Small-displacement, linear-elastic Euler-Bernoulli frame modal preview about the unloaded configuration, with any nonlinear supports at the stated state of a named solved case, with consistent mass on straight members and lumped rigid-body mass on realized arcs and component bodies; numerical integrity does not establish physical correctness.

The integrity checks are numerical estimates under stated premises, not mathematical bounds: each mode's residual is evaluated against a double-double re-formation of the stiffness and mass, its eigenvalue error is a first-order estimate, and the Sturm count is relied on only at shifts where the estimated backward error of forming and factoring the shifted matrix is small against both its estimated distance from singularity and the shift's separation from the computed eigenvalues. They do not bound modelling, discretization or input error.

contents are in all three translational masses and excluded from torsional and rotary inertia (D-e)
loads, temperatures and pressures do not enter the eigenproblem

mass at or coupled to restrained DOFs moves with the supports; fractions are relative to the total mass T_k (X: total 5.558702625335244e1 kg, free-DOF 1.852900875111748e1 kg; Y: total 5.558702625335244e1 kg, free-DOF 0e0 kg; Z: total 5.558702625335244e1 kg, free-DOF 2.0700744566437677e1 kg)

nonlinear supports are linearized at state case `load:SLIDE-POS`'s confirmed converged support states, from its same-run dense_scrutiny solve; the result holds only at those states, and a different operating state gives different frequencies

active one-way and lift-off supports, closed gaps and sticking friction restrain their DOF rigidly, with no finite contact stiffness; an imposed ground or gap value does not enter; inactive and open supports leave their DOF free
a friction support restrains only its tangential DOF; its normal restraint is its own support (or an explicit value) and keeps its own state

friction support `support:NL-F` slides at the state case: its tangential DOF is free with the friction force frozen, contributing no stiffness; this is a modal approximation (the static solver's sliding tangent is nonsymmetric, which a symmetric-definite eigenproblem cannot represent)
